claim: Deep relaxation, a guided practice of about 10 minutes
For deep relaxation, the best results come lying down: lie flat on your back, comfortably, where you won't be physically disturbed for the next, say, 10 minutes or so
To start deep relaxation, eyes open, take a few deep breaths in through the nose and out through the mouth, letting a little of the tension, of that energy inside you, go on each out-breath
In deep relaxation, after the first few deep breaths, on the next exhale close your eyes and mouth, breathe through the nose, and allow your body to breathe
In deep relaxation, feel the weight of your body on the ground: maybe your back, shoulders, back of the hips, heels, hands, arms, head. Let your awareness settle there for a moment
In deep relaxation, let the sounds come and go, with no need to focus on them; be aware of maybe the smells, the air against your skin, and settle into those sensations
In deep relaxation, over the next, say, 15 or 20 seconds, gently and smoothly scan from the top of your head down to your toes, changing nothing, aware of how your body feels

In deep relaxation, rest on your breath, one inhale, one exhale at a time, and count to 10, one on the inhale and two on the exhale. It's okay if your mind wanders: come back to the breath, and start counting over if you'd like, or continue where you left off

In deep relaxation, from your toes and feet, step by step, intentionally let go of a little bit of your body at a time: feet, ankles, maybe calves, hips, back, chest and shoulders, face and jaw, letting face, scalp and jaw sink towards the floor

In deep relaxation, shift to the power of the mind, of visualization, to go deeper: imagine floating above yourself, looking down at your body lying there, your limbs loose, limp, cooked spaghetti noodles, with no desire to move, just resting and settling. See and feel it as much as you can
In deep relaxation, after the spaghetti visualization, a couple of breaths with your awareness back on the breath

In deep relaxation, picture yourself as a marionette doll: your elbows, wrists, knees and hips aren't solid, just connected with loose, limp string. Maybe somebody picks up your leg and it just falls back to the floor. Feel yourself sinking deeper into the floor, towards the earth
In deep relaxation, after the marionette visualization, a couple more nice breaths

In deep relaxation, final visualization: your arms and legs encased in cement, so heavy they sink deeper and deeper into the mattress, on your bed, really or imagined. Maybe somebody walks in, tries to pick up your leg and can't, it's too heavy
Finish deep relaxation with your awareness on your breath for the next 30 seconds or so, sinking into the relaxation you made space for; if your mind wanders, that's okay, bring it back

To end deep relaxation, gently become aware of your surroundings again, the sounds, maybe the air on your skin. Whenever you're ready, open your eyes and, as much as possible, let the physical relaxation continue: a soft, seamless transition into the rest of your day
The guided deep relaxation exercise takes about 10 minutes or so
Done on your own for much longer, 20, 30 or 40 minutes with the same steps and visualizations, the deep relaxation exercise brings "incredible benefits", even greater the longer you do it
